label: At D1, a reward after an unrewarded trial, stronger later in the episode and when S1 is believed good.
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * ep_dec**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * belief_lo ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * (prev_action == 1)
explanation: Only active at D1 (zero at GO/D2). Its magnitude is set by the reward input: near zero after an unrewarded trial, large after a rewarded trial, most of all when the trial before that was unrewarded (a reward following a miss); a second reward in a row gives much less. The reward effect grows with episode time (the timing baseline is additive, so a reward x episode-decile interaction plus a term pulling unrewarded D1 steps down with time carry most of the gain). A smaller graded effect: higher when the ideal observer believes S1 is good (belief_lo), consistent with larger values after a1 rewarded trials. The free fit adds a quadratic time term (activity dips in the last decile) and choice/state of the rewarded trial, gaining little (test 0.233 vs short 0.227). Future variables are not needed. Absolute R^2 beyond timing is low (about 0.23, equal to the profile all-cue ceiling of 0.23) because the activation is sparse and very spiky; short form below 0.25 but captures what additive cues can.
